title: Numbers Chapter 26 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Numbers chapter 26 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Numbers Chapter 26 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Numbers Chapter 26.

questions.question: Who did the LORD speak to after the plague according to Numbers 26?
options: Moses and Eleazar
Aaron and Joshua
Moses and Aaron
Eleazar and Joshua
questions.correctAnswer: Moses and Eleazar
questions.explanation: The LORD spoke unto Moses and unto Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest after the plague, as stated in Numbers 26:1.

questions.question: What age group was counted in the census commanded by the LORD in Numbers 26?
options: From twenty years old and upward
From ten years old and upward
From thirty years old and upward
From five years old and upward
questions.correctAnswer: From twenty years old and upward
questions.explanation: The census was to include all from twenty years old and upward, as commanded by the LORD in Numbers 26:2.

questions.question: Where did Moses and Eleazar speak to the children of Israel to take the census?
options: In the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho
In the wilderness of Sinai
In the land of Canaan
By the Red Sea
questions.correctAnswer: In the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho
questions.explanation: Moses and Eleazar spoke with the children of Israel in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho, according to Numbers 26:3.

questions.question: Which tribe is described as the eldest son of Israel in Numbers 26?
options: Reuben
Simeon
Judah
Gad
questions.correctAnswer: Reuben
questions.explanation: Reuben is described as the eldest son of Israel in Numbers 26:5.

questions.question: How many were numbered of the Reubenites according to the census?
questions.explanation: The number of the Reubenites counted was forty and three thousand seven hundred and thirty (43,730) as stated in Numbers 26:7.

questions.question: Who were the sons of Eliab mentioned in Numbers 26?
options: Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram
Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron
Zerah, Shaul, Jamin
Ard, Naaman, Bela
questions.correctAnswer: Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram
questions.explanation: The sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram as given in Numbers 26:9.

questions.question: True or False: The children of Korah died when the earth swallowed up Korah and his company.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Although Korah and his company died, the children of Korah did not die according to Numbers 26:11.

questions.question: How many were numbered of the Simeonites in the census?
questions.explanation: The Simeonites numbered twenty and two thousand two hundred (22,200) as recorded in Numbers 26:14.

questions.question: True or False: The sons of Judah, Er and Onan, both died in the land of Canaan.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Er and Onan, sons of Judah, died in the land of Canaan as stated in Numbers 26:19.

questions.question: Which family is NOT listed among the sons of Simeon in Numbers 26?
options: Jaminites
Hezronites
Jachinites
Shaulites
questions.correctAnswer: Hezronites
questions.explanation: Hezronites belong to Reuben or Judah, not Simeon. Simeon families include Jaminites, Jachinites, Shaulites, and Nemuelites as per Numbers 26:12-13.

questions.question: According to Numbers 26, who are the families of the children of Gad named after?
options: Zephon, Haggi, Shuni, Ozni, Eri, Arod, Areli
Nemuel, Jamin, Jachin, Zerah, Shaul
Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, Carmi
Shelah, Pharez, Zerah
questions.correctAnswer: Zephon, Haggi, Shuni, Ozni, Eri, Arod, Areli
questions.explanation: These are the families of the children of Gad as listed in Numbers 26:15-17.

questions.question: What was the total number of Judahites counted in the census?
questions.explanation: The number of Judahites was sixty-six thousand and five hundred (66,500) according to Numbers 26:22.

questions.question: In Numbers 26, which comes first in the order of tribes listed: Gad or Simeon?
options: Simeon
Gad
Judah
Reuben
questions.correctAnswer: Simeon
questions.explanation: Simeon is listed before Gad in the order of tribes as seen in Numbers 26:12-15.

questions.question: True or False: Moses and Eleazar numbered the children of Israel in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This is explicitly stated in Numbers 26:3.

questions.question: True or False: The census included all males from one month old and upward.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The census described in Numbers 26:2 included all males from twenty years old and upward, not from one month old.

medium.title: Numbers Chapter 26 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Numbers Chapter 26 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Numbers 26:23-25, which family is NOT listed among the sons of Issachar?
options: Tola
Pua
Jashub
Zerah
questions.correctAnswer: Zerah
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:23-24 lists Tola, Pua, Jashub, and Shimron as families of Issachar, but Zerah is not mentioned among Issachar's families; Zerah belongs to Judah (Numbers 26:20).

questions.question: What does Numbers 26:26-27 reveal about the number of those counted from the tribe of Zebulun?
options: Sixty-four thousand three hundred
Sixty thousand five hundred
Fifty-two thousand seven hundred
Forty-five thousand six hundred
questions.correctAnswer: Sixty thousand five hundred
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:27 states the families of Zebulun numbered sixty thousand and five hundred, distinguishing them from other tribes like Issachar (Numbers 26:25) and Manasseh (Numbers 26:34).

questions.question: What does Numbers 26:28-29 teach us about the sons of Joseph and their families?
options: Joseph had two sons named Manasseh and Ephraim
Joseph had three sons including Gilead
Joseph only had one son named Manasseh
Joseph had a daughter named Sarah
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph had two sons named Manasseh and Ephraim
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:28 clearly states Joseph's sons were Manasseh and Ephraim; Manasseh's descendants include Machir and Gilead (Numbers 26:29), emphasizing the tribal lineage.

questions.question: According to Numbers 26:33, how is Zelophehad's family unique among the families of Manasseh?
options: Zelophehad had no sons but daughters
Zelophehad was the tribe leader
Zelophehad had the largest family
Zelophehad was a priest
questions.correctAnswer: Zelophehad had no sons but daughters
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:33 points out Zelophehad's distinctive situation: he had no sons, only daughters named Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah, highlighting inheritance concerns.

questions.question: What principle about inheritance does God give Moses in Numbers 26:53-56 about dividing the land?
options: Inheritance is divided according to the number of names
Inheritance is given equally regardless of tribe size
Inheritance is only given to Levites
Inheritance is based on seniority of family
questions.correctAnswer: Inheritance is divided according to the number of names
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:53-56 instructs that land inheritance will be divided proportionally according to the number of names in each tribe, with lots determining the specific portion, reflecting fairness and divine order.

questions.question: How does Numbers 26:35-37 demonstrate the concept of family and tribal distinction within Ephraim's descendants?
options: It lists the sons of Shuthelah and their families
It explains Ephraim had no descendants
It shows Ephraim was a Levite
It states Ephraim's family was the largest tribe
questions.correctAnswer: It lists the sons of Shuthelah and their families
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:35-37 details Ephraim's sons after their families, highlighting Shuthelah's family and his son Eran, showing how tribal identity is maintained through family divisions.

questions.question: Based on Numbers 26:38-41, which two sons of Bela founded families within the tribe of Benjamin?
options: Ard and Naaman
Shupham and Hupham
Bela and Ashbel
Ahiram and Shupham
questions.correctAnswer: Ard and Naaman
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:40 specifies that Bela's sons were Ard and Naaman, who each founded families—the Ardites and the Naamites—within Benjamin, showing the subdivision of tribal clans.

questions.question: What does Numbers 26:42-43 teach about the tribe of Dan and the size of the Shuhamite families?
options: The Shuhamites numbered sixty-four thousand four hundred
The tribe of Dan is unnumbered
The Shuhamites were the smallest family
The tribe of Dan had no families
questions.correctAnswer: The Shuhamites numbered sixty-four thousand four hundred
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:43 records that all the families of the Shuhamites, part of Dan, numbered sixty-four thousand four hundred, indicating a significant population within that tribe.

questions.question: True or False: According to Numbers 26:44-47, Asher had a daughter named Sarah mentioned among the families.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:46 explicitly names Sarah as the daughter of Asher, highlighting the mention of female lineage within the tribal record.

questions.question: How does Numbers 26:48-50 emphasize the tribal structure of Naphtali?
options: By listing the families of Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem
By mentioning Naphtali had no families
By focusing only on the number of warriors
By describing Naphtali’s priestly duties
questions.correctAnswer: By listing the families of Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:48-49 lists the families descending from Naphtali's sons, showing the detailed tribal subdivisions and their organization under God’s census.

questions.question: What does Numbers 26:62 say about the Levites and how they were counted compared to other tribes?
options: Levites were counted from a month old but not numbered among Israel
Levites were the largest tribe counted
Levites were excluded from the census entirely
Levites received the largest inheritance
questions.correctAnswer: Levites were counted from a month old but not numbered among Israel
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:62 explains the Levites were counted separately, including males from a month old, but not numbered among Israel because they were not given an inheritance of land.

questions.question: True or False: Numbers 26:65 states that all men numbered by Moses and Aaron in the wilderness of Sinai lived to enter the Promised Land.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:65 clarifies that all men numbered in Sinai died in the wilderness except Caleb and Joshua, showing God’s judgment and faithfulness in preserving only a few.

questions.question: Based on Numbers 26:33-34, what practical lesson about inheritance and God's provision can be drawn from Zelophehad’s daughters?
options: God provides inheritance rights through daughters when no sons are present
Inheritance is only for sons, daughters are excluded
Daughters cannot inherit land in Israel
Zelophehad’s daughters were not named because they inherited nothing
questions.correctAnswer: God provides inheritance rights through daughters when no sons are present
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:33 shows Zelophehad had only daughters, and their names are recorded, indicating God’s provision for inheritance through daughters when no sons exist, a principle expanded in later chapters.

questions.question: How does Numbers 26:53-56 teach about fairness and trust in God's provision in dividing the land?
options: Land is divided by lot but according to tribe size, showing trust in God's fairness
Land is divided equally regardless of tribe size
Land is given only to the largest tribes
Land division is based on personal merit
questions.correctAnswer: Land is divided by lot but according to tribe size, showing trust in God's fairness
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:53-56 describes land division by lot according to tribe size, balancing fairness and trust in God's sovereign provision for each tribe’s inheritance.

questions.question: True or False: Numbers 26:37 records the total number of the sons of Ephraim as thirty-two thousand five hundred.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:37 specifically states that the sons of Ephraim numbered thirty-two thousand five hundred, confirming the census details recorded for the tribe.

hard.title: Numbers Chapter 26 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Numbers Chapter 26.

questions.question: According to Numbers 26, how was the land to be divided among the tribes of Israel?
options: By the size of their armies
According to the number of names and by lot
By the order of birth of the tribe leaders
Equally among all tribes regardless of size
questions.correctAnswer: According to the number of names and by lot
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:53-56 states that the land shall be divided for inheritance according to the number of names, meaning the population of the tribes, and also by lot, distributing between many and few accordingly.

questions.question: Who was the daughter of Asher mentioned in Numbers 26?
options: Mahlah
Sarah
Miriam
Tirzah
questions.correctAnswer: Sarah
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:46 explicitly names Sarah as the daughter of Asher, distinguishing her among the families of Asher.

questions.question: What was unique about the daughters of Zelophehad mentioned in Numbers 26:33 and its significance in Israelite law?
options: They were the first female priests
They inherited their father's property due to lack of sons
They led the tribe of Manasseh in battle
They were forbidden to marry outside their tribe
questions.correctAnswer: They inherited their father's property due to lack of sons
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:33 notes Zelophehad had no sons but daughters, which later in Numbers 27 leads to a legal precedent allowing daughters to inherit if no sons exist, influencing Israelite inheritance laws.

questions.question: How many males from a month old and upward were numbered among the Levites, and why were they not numbered among the children of Israel for inheritance?
options: 23,000; because they were priests
23,000; because they had no inheritance in Israel
12,000; because they were exiled
40,000; because they were warriors
questions.correctAnswer: 23,000; because they had no inheritance in Israel
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:62 explains that 23,000 Levites were counted but not included among the children of Israel for inheritance, as they had no land inheritance among Israel.

questions.question: Which two men were the only survivors from the original wilderness generation according to Numbers 26:65?
options: Moses and Aaron
Caleb and Joshua
Eleazar and Phinehas
Gideon and Barak
questions.correctAnswer: Caleb and Joshua
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:65 states that all who were numbered in Sinai died in the wilderness, except Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun, who survived to enter the Promised Land.

questions.question: What is the significance of the numbering of the tribes in Numbers 26 in relation to the previous census in Numbers 1?
options: It shows a decrease in Israel's population
It reflects a new generation prepared to enter Canaan
It records the tribes after their conquest of Canaan
It counts only the Levites
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects a new generation prepared to enter Canaan
questions.explanation: Numbers 26, compared to Numbers 1, counts the new generation after the plague and wilderness wanderings, emphasizing those able to go to war and enter the Promised Land, as earlier generation died (Numbers 26:64-65).

questions.question: Which family did Korah, who rebelled against Moses and Aaron, belong to, and what happened to his followers?
options: The Kohathites; swallowed by the earth
The Gershonites; exiled to Egypt
The Merarites; burned by fire
The Levites; banished
questions.correctAnswer: The Kohathites; swallowed by the earth
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:9-10 tells of Dathan and Abiram, followers of Korah from the family of Kohath, who were swallowed up by the earth as a sign of God's judgment against their rebellion.

questions.question: True or False: According to Numbers 26, the Levites were assigned a portion of the land as an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:62 states that the Levites were not numbered among the children of Israel for land inheritance because they were not given a territorial inheritance.

questions.question: True or False: The total number of Israelites counted in Numbers 26 was over 600,000 men able to go to war.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:51 reports the total number of the children of Israel counted as six hundred thousand and a thousand seven hundred and thirty, indicating a large, war-capable population.

questions.question: Which tribe had the largest number of men counted in Numbers 26?
options: Judah
Reuben
Gad
Dan
questions.correctAnswer: Judah
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:22 shows Judah had 76,500 men, the largest number among the tribes, reflecting its prominence and fulfilling Jacob's blessing in Genesis 49:8-12.

questions.question: What literary device is demonstrated by the repeated listing of families and their numbers in Numbers 26?
options: Chiasm
Inclusion
Parallelism
Typology
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Numbers 26 uses parallelism in its structure by repeating the pattern of naming a tribe, its families, and their numbers, emphasizing order and completeness in the census.

questions.question: The name 'Eleazar' appears in Numbers 26 in what relation to Aaron, and what is his significance?
options: Son of Aaron; succeeded him as high priest
Brother of Aaron; led the Levites
Father of Aaron; ancestor of Moses
Cousin of Aaron; rebelled with Korah
questions.correctAnswer: Son of Aaron; succeeded him as high priest
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:1 and 26:60 identify Eleazar as Aaron's son, who played a priestly role and would later succeed Aaron as high priest, maintaining the priestly line.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes the theme of land inheritance division by lot as stated in Numbers 26?
options: Joshua 18:10
Exodus 20:12
Leviticus 25:23
Deuteronomy 6:5
questions.correctAnswer: Joshua 18:10
questions.explanation: Joshua 18:10 describes the casting of lots for the division of the land among the tribes, directly echoing the instructions given in Numbers 26:55-56 about inheritance by lot.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word "Mahlah," one of Zelophehad's daughters, and how might it relate to the theme of inheritance?
options: "Sickness"; representing struggle
"Sickness"; highlighting the family's hardship
"Weakness"; showing vulnerability
"Strength"; showing resilience
questions.correctAnswer: "Sickness"; highlighting the family's hardship
questions.explanation: The Hebrew name Mahlah means "sickness," which may symbolize the hardship Zelophehad's family faced due to lack of male heirs, linking to the chapter's concern with inheritance rights (Numbers 26:33).

questions.question: Which tribe's families are listed as including the Jaminites and Zarhites in Numbers 26?
options: Simeon
Reuben
Judah
Issachar
questions.correctAnswer: Simeon
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:12-13 lists the families of Simeon, including the Nemuelites, Jaminites, and Zarhites, showing the tribe's subdivisions.

theological.title: Numbers Chapter 26 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Numbers Chapter 26 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Numbers 26:10 reveal about God's judgment and holiness?
options: God’s judgment is immediate and decisive against rebellion
God is indifferent to human rebellion
God delays judgment to give more chances
God’s judgment is symbolic but not real
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is immediate and decisive against rebellion
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:10 describes how the earth swallowed Dathan and Abiram with Korah when they rebelled, demonstrating God’s immediate and decisive judgment against sin and rebellion, affirming His holiness and justice.

questions.question: According to Numbers 26:55, how is the land inheritance divided among the tribes of Israel?
options: By lot, according to the names of the tribes
By the size of the tribe alone
By the age of the tribe’s leader
By the tribe’s military strength
questions.correctAnswer: By lot, according to the names of the tribes
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:55 teaches that the land inheritance is divided by lot according to the names of the tribes, showing God’s sovereign ordination in allotting the promised land fairly among Israel.

questions.question: What theological truth is taught by the numbering of the Levites separately from the other tribes in Numbers 26:62?
options: The Levites had no inheritance among the Israelites
The Levites were the richest tribe
The Levites were excluded from God’s covenant
The Levites were the only tribe allowed to fight
questions.correctAnswer: The Levites had no inheritance among the Israelites
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:62 states that the Levites were numbered separately because they had no inheritance among the Israelites, indicating their unique role as priests and mediators, dependent on God rather than land for provision.

questions.question: How does the census in Numbers 26:51 reflect God’s providential care and faithfulness to Israel?
options: The total number shows God preserved a vast and renewed nation
The number was insignificant and disappointing
The census was conducted by men, not God
The census focused only on women
questions.correctAnswer: The total number shows God preserved a vast and renewed nation
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:51 records a total of over 600,000 men able to go to war, after the plague, showing God's providence in preserving and renewing Israel despite prior judgments, demonstrating His faithfulness to His covenant people.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about divine justice and mercy is drawn from comparing Numbers 26:10 and Numbers 26:11?
options: God judges rebels but preserves the faithful among them
God punishes all equally without exception
God shows no mercy to any sinners
God ignores the consequences of sin
questions.correctAnswer: God judges rebels but preserves the faithful among them
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:10 shows the judgment on Korah’s company, while verse 11 notes that the children of Korah did not die, illustrating God’s justice against sin but mercy toward the faithful remnant within a sinful group.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted by God’s command to Moses and Eleazar to number those able to go to war in Numbers 26:2?
options: God’s sovereignty over Israel’s organization and military strength
God’s ignorance of Israel’s numbers
God’s partiality to certain tribes
God’s neglect of military matters
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereignty over Israel’s organization and military strength
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:2 shows God directing the census of those able to go to war, emphasizing His sovereign control over Israel’s structure and preparedness for conquest, reflecting His providential rule.

questions.question: How does Numbers 26:65 contribute to the narrative arc of God's covenant faithfulness despite Israel’s failures?
options: Only Caleb and Joshua survived from the previous generation, preserving the covenant line
All the older generation was preserved without exception
God abandoned Israel completely after the wilderness
Moses and Aaron were also excluded from the promise
questions.correctAnswer: Only Caleb and Joshua survived from the previous generation, preserving the covenant line
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:65 shows that while the older generation perished due to disobedience, God preserved Caleb and Joshua, ensuring the continuity of His covenant promises and the eventual fulfillment of the land inheritance, fitting into the redemptive narrative.

questions.question: What doctrinal teaching about inheritance and divine justice emerges from combining Numbers 26:53 and Numbers 26:56?
options: Inheritance is allotted fairly by divine lot, respecting tribal population
Inheritance is given randomly without justice
Inheritance is based on human strength alone
Inheritance is irrelevant in God’s plan
questions.correctAnswer: Inheritance is allotted fairly by divine lot, respecting tribal population
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:53 and 26:56 together teach that God commands the land to be divided by lot according to tribe names and population size, showing divine justice and fairness in allotting blessings according to His sovereign plan.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the census in Numbers 26 is an exaggeration and unreliable. What does Numbers 26:3-4 actually teach about God’s command and the purpose of this census?
options: The census was a direct command from God for an accurate count of fighting men
The census was a human invention without divine authority
The census was symbolic and not intended to be accurate
The census was only for taxation purposes
questions.correctAnswer: The census was a direct command from God for an accurate count of fighting men
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:3-4 records God speaking to Moses and Eleazar commanding a census from age twenty and upward, showing the census was divinely mandated with a clear purpose, countering sceptical claims of exaggeration or inaccuracy.

questions.question: What theological significance is found in the mention of Zelophehad’s daughters in Numbers 26:33 regarding inheritance rights?
options: It foreshadows God’s provision for inheritance through daughters when no sons exist
It denies women any inheritance rights
It shows daughters were excluded from family lineage
It teaches that inheritance is only spiritual
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows God’s provision for inheritance through daughters when no sons exist
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:33 mentions Zelophehad’s daughters, highlighting God’s recognition of their claim to inheritance in the absence of sons, revealing His justice and provision, which is later fully legislated in Numbers 27.

questions.question: How does Numbers 26:59-60 reveal God’s providential preparation for priestly leadership in Israel?
options: It names Jochebed as mother of Aaron, Moses, and Miriam, establishing the priestly line
It states that priests were chosen randomly
It denies any special lineage for priests
It shows priests were from the tribe of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: It names Jochebed as mother of Aaron, Moses, and Miriam, establishing the priestly line
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:59-60 names Amram’s wife Jochebed as mother of Aaron, Moses, and Miriam, emphasizing the providential and familial establishment of the priestly leadership crucial for Israel’s worship and covenant life.

questions.question: What combined teaching about God’s covenant faithfulness and judgment is seen in Numbers 26:64-65 and Numbers 26:1-2?
options: God judges the unfaithful but preserves a faithful remnant for covenant fulfillment
God destroys all without distinction
God’s covenant is conditional on human works alone
God’s promises are void due to Israel’s rebellion
questions.correctAnswer: God judges the unfaithful but preserves a faithful remnant for covenant fulfillment
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:1-2 initiates the census after the plague judgment, while 26:64-65 notes all who sinned were dead except Caleb and Joshua, showing God’s justice in judgment and His covenant faithfulness in preserving a remnant to inherit the land.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by His command in Numbers 26:57-58 to number the Levite families separately?
options: God’s holiness in setting apart the Levites for priestly service
God’s forgetfulness regarding the Levites
God’s partiality against the Levites
God’s indifference to tribal distinctions
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness in setting apart the Levites for priestly service
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:57-58 shows God’s command to number the Levite families separately, reflecting His holiness in designating them as a distinct, consecrated tribe devoted to priestly duties.

questions.question: How does Numbers 26:19-21 contribute to the theological understanding of judgment and mercy within the tribe of Judah?
options: Er and Onan died in Canaan, but their brothers’ families continued, showing both judgment and preservation
Er and Onan thrived and led the tribe
Judah was untouched by God’s judgment
All of Judah’s sons died without descendants
questions.correctAnswer: Er and Onan died in Canaan, but their brothers’ families continued, showing both judgment and preservation
questions.explanation: Numbers 26:19-21 notes that Er and Onan died, but Judah’s lineage continued through Shelah, Pharez, and Zerah, illustrating God’s just judgment on individuals and His mercy in preserving the tribe’s covenant line.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God’s providence and human responsibility is taught by the detailed family listings and census numbers throughout Numbers 26?
options: God sovereignly orders His people’s inheritance, requiring faithful obedience
God leaves the inheritance to chance without guidance
Human effort alone secures God’s promises
Numbers are irrelevant to God’s plan
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly orders His people’s inheritance, requiring faithful obedience
questions.explanation: The detailed census in Numbers 26 records God’s sovereign ordering of the tribes’ inheritance based on families and numbers, highlighting the necessary human faithfulness within God’s providential plan for covenant fulfillment.
